name: Hangzhou Zhonhen Electric Co., Ltd.
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Zhonhen Electric is China's data-center HVDC power leader — #1 at 31% share per Kezhi Consulting's 2025 count, the co-developer of Alibaba's Panama power architecture, and the lead drafter of the national 240V/336V DC standard — now converting that fifteen-year domestic franchise into an 800VDC/AI story while CATL pays RMB 4.1B for 49% of its controlling holdco; the unpublished H1 2026 report (due by 31 August 2026) is the near-term checkpoint. BACKGROUND: Founded 1996 in Hangzhou by Zhu Guoding; listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange March 2010. Four reported businesses: data-center power (36.3% of FY2025 revenue), telecom/station energy, grid power-supply systems, and power-digitalization software via subsidiary Beijing Zhonhen Borui, plus an EV charging line. FY2025 revenue RMB 2.137B (+8.9%), attributable net profit RMB 126.4M (+15.3%) — a miss against the ~RMB 164M institutional consensus, per company filings and consensus data from Tonghuashun (the Chinese financial-data platform 10jqka.com.cn). Exports were 4.1% of FY2025 revenue; overseas expansion runs through Singapore — wholly-owned Enervell Power Pte. Ltd. (est. 2024) and the 20%-held SuperX Digital Power JV (est. September 2025, mandate: global HVDC excluding Greater China). Governance requires explicit note: founder and actual controller Zhu Guoding (40.12% voting control) was convicted of securities-market manipulation by the Hangzhou Intermediate Court on 31 December 2025 (three years imprisonment suspended for four, RMB 1M fine); he resigned the chair in 2021 and holds no board or officer seat. His wife Bao Xiaoru has chaired the company since November 2021. Collection gap: no H1 2026 report or profit alert as of 22 August 2026, nine days before the filing deadline.
ecosystemRole: We assess Zhonhen as the strongest pure claim on the thesis that NVIDIA's 800VDC transition validates an architecture China already runs at scale — its Panama one-stage 10kV-to-DC conversion predates the Western 800VDC push by six years, and its BAT/operator installed base is the largest HVDC field record anywhere. That validation is now explicit rather than inferred: NVIDIA's August 2026 execution paper names the Panama Architecture as a transformer-rectifier-unit implementation of its own data-hall DC power block (pp. 21–23). Architectural endorsement and commercial inclusion remain separate questions, and only the first has been answered. For US-facing AIDC work its relevance is prospective, not present: exports are 4.1% of revenue, no US entity is on record, it is absent from NVIDIA's published 800VDC partner rosters (whose power-component tier names Delta, Flex Power, Lead Wealth, LiteOn and Megmeet — Hopewind, contrary to Chinese trade coverage, is not on NVIDIA's lists either), and the company itself denied signed agreements with NVIDIA, Meta or Google in August 2025. The competitive read-through: Zhonhen entering the West via the Enervell/SuperX structure tests whether a Chinese HVDC incumbent can sell architecture leadership into markets whose policy stack is being built to exclude Chinese electronics.

productsAndServices.name: Data-center power — HVDC, Panama and 800V
productsAndServices.description: The core franchise (RMB 775.8M, 36.3% of FY2025 revenue, +16.1%): a grid-to-chip DC power matrix spanning HVDC systems (380VAC to 240V/336V/800V DC, ≥97.5% efficiency, batteries hung directly on the DC busbar for zero-interruption ride-through), Panama power (one-stage conversion of 10kV directly to 240V/400V/800V DC, collapsing the traditional four-level chain to one, >97.5% system efficiency), prefabricated Panama power modules (P/H/AC series integrating 10kV distribution, transformer, UPS and output distribution; 2.5MW IT load per system), precision row-level distribution cabinets, and server PSUs. Per company filings.
highlights: Independently ranked #1 in China intelligent-computing-center HVDC at 31% share, CR3 72% (Kezhi Consulting 2025, via Ajian Securities); pioneer credit is documented — first-generation 240V DC system in 2010, lead drafter of the national 240V/336V DC standard, MIIT Manufacturing Single-Item Champion 2022

Panama power co-developed with Alibaba; FY2025 wins include Alibaba Panama 2.0/STS/ATS systems, Tencent elastic DC systems, ByteDance precision distribution, Bank of China HVDC, and an 800V DC microgrid project with China Mobile Energy — per the FY2025 annual report

Panama-800V medium-voltage rectifier series shown at IDCC2025 in three architectures (2N, N+1, and a DR four-bus design the company describes as optimized for NVIDIA SuperPOD-class GPU servers); won the 2025 China IDC Industry Innovation Technology Product Award; company claims vs traditional distributed systems: footprint −50%, construction cost −30%, deployment 50% faster

TÜV Rheinland Bauart Mark/CE certification for AIDC power products (January 2026) — company states it is the first AIDC power maker in Greater China to hold it, framed explicitly as the gateway for international expansion

Not on NVIDIA's published 800VDC partner rosters (whose component tier names Delta, Flex Power, Lead Wealth, LiteOn and Megmeet; Hopewind appears only in Chinese trade coverage, not on NVIDIA's own lists), and the company denied signed agreements with NVIDIA/Meta/Google in its 19 August 2025 abnormal-fluctuation clarification — the architecture-compatibility claims are the company's own
productsAndServices.positioning: Domestic HVDC leader ahead of Kehua Data (whose 800V order momentum is independently reported to be narrowing the gap), Delta China and Vertiv; in traditional UPS the market belongs to Delta, Vertiv and Schneider. Differentiation is architecture incumbency: fifteen years of DC-for-data-centers field history and the Alibaba co-development record, against rivals arriving at DC power from the UPS side.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: 100% direct sales per the FY2025 annual report; top-5 customers 14.34% of sales; hyperscaler and operator centralized procurement
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Intelligent-computing and supercomputing centers, internet platforms (Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance), third-party colocation, telecom operators, financial and government data centers
productsAndServices.roadmap: 2026 plan per the annual report: enrich the 800V DC product system and complete global certifications; an 800V smart-computing reference-design white paper was announced at IDCC2025 (December 2025)

productsAndServices.name: Enervell and the SuperX Digital Power JV
productsAndServices.description: The overseas structure has two layers: Enervell Power Pte. Ltd. (Singapore, wholly-owned, est. 2024) — the international brand covering IDC power, telecom/5G power, new-power-system equipment and EV charging — and SuperX Digital Power Pte. Ltd. (est. September 2025), a JV with Nasdaq-listed Super X AI Technology covering global HVDC excluding mainland China/HK/Macau, in which Enervell holds 20% and entities controlled by overseas-business co-heads Zhu Yikun and Xu Feifei hold 10% each. Per SZSE announcement 2025-47 and the SuperX SEC 6-K.
highlights: JV launched two 800V products on 31 October 2025: SuperX Panama-800VDC (new-build, up to 3.6MW, 98.5% peak efficiency, conversion stages cut from 4–5 to 1–2, copper −45% vs AC, supports 1MW+ cabinets; company states compatibility with NVIDIA's Kyber architecture) and SuperX Aurora-800VDC (live-retrofit for existing data centers)
SuperX bears the JV's necessary operating costs for three years; CEO jointly appointed by SuperX and Enervell — an unusually low-capital route to an overseas channel
Caveat per third-party record: SuperX (Nasdaq: SUPX) converted from an interior-design services firm into an AI-infrastructure company; the JV is the NVIDIA-adjacent linkage retail narratives lean on

No US entity, USPTO trademark or US hiring evidence found as of 18 August 2026; overseas exports were 4.1% of FY2025 revenue (RMB 87.6M, +178%) via EPC channels (Saudi plant DC systems, Germany 3MW hydrogen, Egypt Suez 1.1GW wind)
productsAndServices.positioning: Entering Western and Southeast Asian AIDC power against Vertiv, Eaton, Schneider, Delta and the ODM tier — with architecture claims and cost position but no local certification base, service network or reference installations outside China
productsAndServices.soldThrough: JV channel (SuperX brand) plus Enervell direct/OEM; the international site offers white-label power modules
productsAndServices.targetSegments: AI data centers in Southeast Asia, the Middle East and — prospectively — North America
productsAndServices.roadmap: Global certifications named as the 2026 gating item in the annual report; TÜV CE certification (Jan 2026) is the first completed step

productsAndServices.name: Telecom and station energy
productsAndServices.description: Modular power systems to 600A, integrated energy cabinets accepting mains/PV/diesel/wind inputs with DC48V/AC220V/DC280V outputs ('one cabinet, one station'), and distributed PV-storage — RMB 384.2M of FY2025 revenue (+25.8%, 26.75% gross margin). Long-term China Mobile and China Tower relationships; FY2025 wins include China Tower modular-power central procurement and the China Telecom 2025–2027 combined switching-power procurement; a 6G zero-carbon base-station pilot installed 2025. Per the FY2025 annual report.
highlights: Front-rank share in operator centralized procurement (company claim)
Modular power 4.0 (open, cloud-architecture) named as the roadmap direction

productsAndServices.name: Grid power-supply systems
productsAndServices.description: AC low-voltage switchgear, substation DC systems, power-communication power, power UPS/inverters and new-energy DC products for State Grid, Southern Grid and power plants — RMB 473.7M of FY2025 revenue (−1.1%, 24.19% gross margin). FY2025 wins include State Grid UHV projects and export deliveries through EPC channels: Saudi power-plant DC systems, a 3MW hydrogen-production system in Germany, and Egypt's 1.1GW Suez wind project. Per the FY2025 annual report.
highlights: The stable legacy base that funds the AIDC push
Exports ride other companies' EPC scope rather than an own channel

productsAndServices.name: EV charging and battery swap
productsAndServices.description: High-power DC charging: 60–640kW integrated dual-gun chargers, 360–2500kW split charging stacks with liquid-cooled 800A supercharge terminals, Panama 800V direct-on-DC-bus charging (320–480kW integrated, 1200–2400kW split), megawatt chargers for swap stations, and V2G. Customers include State Grid, Sinopec, China Tower, CNOOC; custom high-power equipment supplied to Envision Energy and CATL's charging-service arm Times Electric Service branded stations. Per the FY2025 annual report.
highlights: Not a ranked player in China's charging-module market (top-5 lists are Infypower, UUGreenPower, Yonglian, Tonhe, Increase) — Zhonhen sells equipment and stacks, not merchant modules
The CATL strategic cooperation names charging/swap as one of three collaboration domains, via subsidiary Zhonhen Yunqi Energy

productsAndServices.name: Power digitalization software (Beijing Zhonhen Borui)
productsAndServices.description: The highest-margin segment (RMB 418.9M FY2025 revenue, +7.3%, 34.58% gross margin; subsidiary net profit RMB 32.1M): power-market trading and virtual-power-plant platforms covering all provincial spot-market rules, relay-protection setting calculation, grid planning and line-loss management, power data/project-management AI tools, integrated-energy services and simulation/digital-twin analytics, sold to State Grid, Southern Grid, gencos, petrochemical, nuclear and data centers. Per the FY2025 annual report.
highlights: 20 spot-trading projects delivered in FY2025; VPP pilots in 10+ provinces
The CATL strategic cooperation names power trading ('compute-electricity coordination') as a collaboration domain running through Borui

specs.label: Rack support
specs.value: 1MW+ single cabinets; 250kW+ GPU racks; stated NVIDIA Kyber compatibility

technicalSpecs.notes: Launched 31 October 2025 with SuperX Aurora-800VDC, a modular live-retrofit variant for existing halls. Figures are company/JV claims; no third-party test data published. Interface note (August 2026): NVIDIA's execution paper sizes its data-hall DC power block at approximately 4.8MW and expects it to be assembled from paralleled rectifier modules, so a 3.6MW Panama-800VDC system is a sub-block building element rather than a one-for-one substitute for a block.

technicalSpecs.notes: The architecture that replaced UPS in Chinese internet data centers; Zhonhen led the national standard for it. 'HVDC' here is data-center DC distribution, not grid transmission HVDC.
Megawatt-class chargers for battery-swap stations; V2G bidirectional units on the international site.

recentDevelopments.headline: NVIDIA's second 800VDC white paper (Industry Alignment & Execution) names the Panama Architecture as a transformer-rectifier-unit implementation of its data-hall DC power block, describes TRU-based blocks as highly practical at roughly the 5MW class and already in initial implementation, and dates next-generation solid-state transformers to around 2029
recentDevelopments.read: The first appearance of the architecture Zhonhen co-developed, by name, in an NVIDIA engineering document. It confers no commercial relationship — Zhonhen remains off every published partner roster — but it retires the argument that the Panama approach sits outside the Western reference design, and it puts a clock on the opening: TRU-based blocks ship now, their solid-state successor is roughly three years out.
recentDevelopments.source: NVIDIA, 800 VDC Architecture: Industry Alignment & Execution (August 2026), pp. 21–23

recentDevelopments.headline: CATL signs definitive agreements: RMB 4.099B (RMB 3.512B cash + a 49% stake in Times Tianyuan valued RMB 588M) for 49% of controlling holdco Zhonhen Technology Investment; Zhu Guoding remains actual controller (35.7% of holdco post-deal, wife Bao Xiaoru 15.3%); same-day strategic cooperation across computing-power infrastructure, charging/swap and power trading
recentDevelopments.read: The 'compute-electricity coordination' bet lands at the holdco, not the listco — CATL gains nomination rights to one listco director, one deputy GM and a finance-department manager while the family keeps control; closing within six months.

recentDevelopments.headline: EGM approves the third employee stock ownership plan: up to RMB 40M, ≤40 participants, buyback shares at RMB 21.79 (half the market average), with unlock hurdles of revenue +30%/+70%/+120% vs FY2025 (or profit alternatives) across 2026–2028
recentDevelopments.read: Management's own ambition curve: the hurdles imply roughly RMB 2.8B/3.6B/4.7B revenue — a doubling in three years that only the AIDC line can plausibly deliver.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q1 2026: revenue RMB 418.4M (+7.8%), net profit RMB 24.9M (+22.9%); inventory +37.9% vs year-end on stocking for shipments; short-term borrowings up ~14x to RMB 224M
recentDevelopments.read: The inventory and borrowing build reads as ramp preparation ahead of H1 deliveries — the H1 report (due by 31 August 2026) is the verification point.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2025: revenue RMB 2.137B (+8.9%), attributable net profit RMB 126.4M (+15.3%) — below the ~RMB 164M three-institution consensus; data-center power RMB 775.8M (+16.1%); FY2025 wins include Alibaba Panama 2.0/STS/ATS, Tencent elastic DC, ByteDance precision distribution
recentDevelopments.read: Revenue in line, profit a 20–25% miss against consensus — the AIDC narrative ran ahead of the income statement for a second straight year.

recentDevelopments.headline: CATL framework agreement announced: intent to acquire 49% of the controlling holdco at a ~43.5% premium to appraised value
recentDevelopments.read: First public confirmation of the CATL tie-up after months of market speculation; the definitive terms landed four months later with a different cash/equity split.

recentDevelopments.headline: TÜV Rheinland Bauart Mark / CE certification for AIDC power products — claimed first among Greater China AIDC power manufacturers
recentDevelopments.read: The first completed step of the 2026 'global certifications' plan; a prerequisite for selling prefabricated HVDC outside China, not a differentiator inside it.

recentDevelopments.headline: Founder and actual controller Zhu Guoding convicted of securities-market manipulation by Hangzhou Intermediate Court: three years imprisonment suspended for four, RMB 1M fine; company states he holds no director/officer role and operations are unaffected
recentDevelopments.read: The largest single governance fact on file — he retains 40.12% voting control, and the CATL deal eight months later was structured around him remaining actual controller.

recentDevelopments.headline: Eighth-anniversary strategic partnership signing with ABB (China) Electrification covering HVDC, 800V DC for AI computing and global expansion
recentDevelopments.read: A Western-incumbent channel relationship that predates the AI cycle — notable because ABB is simultaneously building its own medium-voltage AIDC power franchise.

recentDevelopments.headline: Panama-800V medium-voltage rectifier series presented at IDCC2025 in three architectures including a DR four-bus design described as optimized for NVIDIA SuperPOD-class GPU servers; wins 2025 China IDC Industry Innovation Technology Product Award; 800V reference-design white paper announced
recentDevelopments.read: The domestic 800V flagship moment — architecture claims are the company's own; NVIDIA has not listed Zhonhen among its 800VDC partners.

recentDevelopments.headline: SuperX Digital Power JV launches SuperX Panama-800VDC (3.6MW, 98.5% peak efficiency, stated NVIDIA Kyber compatibility) and SuperX Aurora-800VDC (live retrofit)
recentDevelopments.read: The overseas product line exists five weeks after the JV was formed — speed enabled by rebadging the domestic Panama stack under a Singapore JV brand.
recentDevelopments.source: Company news, hzzh.com, 2025-10-31; Ajian Securities initiation

recentDevelopments.headline: SuperX Digital Power Pte. Ltd. JV formed with Nasdaq-listed Super X AI Technology (40%), Enervell (20%), entities of overseas co-heads Zhu Yikun (10%) and Xu Feifei (10%), and a Singaporean investor (20%); mandate is global HVDC excluding Greater China; SuperX bears operating costs for three years
recentDevelopments.read: The overseas vehicle binds the controller's son and the GM with personal equity — incentive alignment that also routes overseas upside partly outside the listed company.

recentDevelopments.headline: Abnormal-fluctuation clarification after the stock rose >20% in three sessions: rumors of partnerships with NVIDIA, Meta and Google are false; no cooperation agreements or sales contracts signed with these overseas cloud vendors
recentDevelopments.read: The stock trades on an AI-export narrative the company itself has formally disavowed — any Western-partnership claim after this date needs primary-source verification.

recentDevelopments.headline: Co-organizes China's first 800V DC power seminar for intelligent-computing centers with the communications-industry ICT-energy committee; founder Zhu Guoding commits continued 800V R&D investment
recentDevelopments.read: Standard-setting is the incumbent's playbook — the same route it used to own the 240V/336V specification a decade earlier.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Zhonhen's domestic HVDC leadership as real and structural, not narrative. Basis: independent share data (Kezhi Consulting 2025: #1 at 31%, CR3 72%), lead authorship of the national 240V/336V DC standard, MIIT single-champion designation, the Alibaba Panama co-development record, and FY2025 wins spanning Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, Bank of China and China Mobile Energy. Customer-validation cycles of three-plus years function as the moat.

(High confidence) We assess the 800VDC/AI transition as double-edged for Zhonhen: it globally validates the DC-for-compute architecture the company pioneered, yet re-opens domestic competition and exposes its absence from the Western ecosystem. Basis: Kehua Data's independently reported 800V order momentum 'narrowing the gap'; NVIDIA's published 800VDC partner rosters naming Delta and Megmeet among mainland-linked vendors but not Zhonhen; the company's own August 2025 denial of NVIDIA/Meta/Google agreements. Updated August 2026: NVIDIA's execution paper names the Panama Architecture in its own engineering text (pp. 21–23) while the vendor rosters still omit the company — the sharpest available statement of the split between architectural credit and commercial access.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the overseas expansion as deliberately structured for speed and insulation rather than commitment: a Singapore brand (Enervell), a JV whose Nasdaq-listed partner bears three years of operating costs, and personal 10% stakes for the controller's son and the GM. This binds the family's next generation to the international outcome but keeps the listco's capital exposure minimal — and routes part of any overseas upside outside the listed company. US footprint as of August 2026: no entity, no certifications beyond TÜV CE, exports 4.1% of revenue.

(High confidence) We assess the CATL transaction as a re-rating of what Zhonhen is: RMB 4.1B for 49% of the holdco, with nomination rights reaching into listco management, converts a data-center power vendor into the equipment arm of a 'compute-electricity coordination' platform spanning AIDC power, charging/swap and power trading. Basis: the definitive agreements and strategic-cooperation scope of 14 August 2026.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that a governance and quality discount is warranted alongside the growth story. Basis: the founder's December 2025 manipulation conviction; receivables at roughly nine times profit with negative Q1 operating cash flow; a FY2025 profit miss against consensus; and a stock that required a formal rumor denial in August 2025. Indicator to watch: the H1 2026 report (due by 31 August 2026) — data-center power revenue growth and cash conversion are the tests of whether the ESOP hurdles (+30% revenue in 2026) are credible.

(Moderate confidence) We assess Zhonhen's Western go-to-market as aimed at AI-native cloud operators rather than at the hyperscalers or the retail colocation base — and that the split inside that segment matters more than the target list. Basis: first-hand context relayed to us by the company's commercial side in August 2026 — unsourced, not a public statement — that speed of deployment and technical capability outrank incumbency in its customer screen; set against the public record, which divides the category sharply. Operators that build and own their halls control the medium-voltage-to-DC decision this product addresses; operators that lease shells from colocation landlords can influence rack-side choices only, whatever their compute scale. Indicator to watch: whether the first Enervell or SuperX reference customer outside Greater China is a self-building operator or a tenant.

periods.commentary: Data-center power revenue RMB 668M (+111%) drove the year, rising from 21% to 34% of revenue. Operating cash flow RMB 468M.

Gross margin pressure (9M 2025 −2.84pp) and receivables growth (RMB 1.01B at Q3, ~9x profit) accompanied the growth; operating cash flow fell 48% to RMB 243M. Exports RMB 87.6M (+178%) — 4.1% of revenue.

financials.commentary: The structural pattern: revenue and the AIDC mix advance while profit quality lags — consensus misses, thin cash conversion, heavy receivables. The CATL holdco investment (RMB 4.1B, definitive August 2026) and the ESOP-3 hurdles define the bull case management itself has signed up for.
